transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-08 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Ramos (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Crestline), Maya Singh (Crestline SRE), Jared Vega (CTO), Hannah Park (Network)
---
Auto-summary (auto-generated): Went over kernel-induced latency spikes after last kernel bump; identified possible egress MTU/fragmentation issues with customer's VPC NAT gateway; agreed to run controlled canary and share detailed traces.
---
00:00 Alex Ramos: ok everyone thanks for joining, uh quick agenda, uh recap of last week's tests, tuning experiments we ran, egress shaping results and then next steps, sound good?
00:12 Liam O'Connor: yep thanks Alex, wanted to start with the the throughput regression, we saw a 12% p99 increase after the kernel upgrade on your side, and then an intermittent stall on longer sequences, not sure yet if it's our networking or the runtime change.
00:28 Priya Nair: yeah so we rolled kernel 1.4.3 and we saw elevated tail latency for sequences >1k tokens in a couple of pods, we put a canary back to 1.4.1 and p99 dropped pretty close to baseline, so it's strongly correlated but not yet causally proven.
00:47 Maya Singh: there was also some packet reassembly errors in our NAT logs around the same window, we captured a few  tcp fragments that looked odd, could be MTU mismatch or path MTU, hmm.
01:05 Priya Nair: ok that's useful, thanks Maya, did you notice if it's only on inter-AZ traffic or intra-AZ?
01:12 Hannah Park: looks like inter-AZ egress to the siloed inference subnets, the NAT gateway sits in a public subnet and then routes to our VPC peering — we did see 1k-1.4k sized packets getting fragmented, we suspect the Azure/OCI overlay is doing something weird at peak.
01:31 Jared Vega: just to add context, our production SLAs are tight here, if we lose 10% of requests at p99 that's customer-facing. We need a clear rollback and fallback policy.
01:42 Alex Ramos: agreed, so short term contingency is routing fallback: if p99 crosses threshold we'll route to hosted Redwood pool in us-west-2 for warm-prefill and fall back for tails—this is in the runbook but we need to test the routing policy end-to-end.
02:02 Jordan Li: I can coordinate the routing policy test, we have a toggle in the control plane but we need the customer's routing tag to match — Liam can you confirm which tag you want us to watch for?
02:14 Liam O'Connor: we'll use tag crestline-staging-2026-10, I'll add that to the insp config later today.
02:20 Priya Nair: on the telemetry side we noticed gaps: when the kernel bump happened, some spans from the runtime didn't make it into their Prometheus scrape window, and trace IDs got dropped. We need full request-level traces to map KV cache misses to egress events.
02:39 Maya Singh: yeah our tracing pipeline truncated some logs at 5MB, which may have dropped the tail spans. We'll increase retention temporarily.
02:49 Alex Ramos: good. Also there's an outstanding ask around the quantization rollback experiment: we reverted to FP16 on two nodes and that improved throughput by 6% but memory hit went up — thoughts?
03:05 Priya Nair: quantization affects kernel code paths, so combined with a kernel change you may see odd slowdowns; it's safest to isolate variables: either kernel 1.4.1 + quantized, or kernel 1.4.3 + non-quantized and compare. We'll spin both combos in a short AB run.
03:22 Liam O'Connor: timeline? we can run AB overnight.
03:26 Priya Nair: Redwood will schedule the AB starting 02:00 UTC tomorrow and run for 2 hours steady-state, capture token-level latencies and KV cache hit rates.
03:33 Hannah Park: for the egress side I will pull packet-capture for the window when we saw the stalled requests and dropbox it. Could be overlay issue as I said.
03:42 Alex Ramos: great, please include timestamps and the NAT gateway IDs.
03:48 Jared Vega: security question: does the hosted fallback route touch any PII? we need a short brief for security team about egress controls and KMS.
03:57 Jordan Li: the hosted fallback will redteam only use obfuscated payloads in the test, and for production we can enable token scrubbing and customer-managed KMS per the Private plan. We'll share the security checklist.
04:11 Alex Ramos: Priya will send the SOC2 excerpt and the network segmentation doc after the call.
04:18 Maya Singh: small nit, when we enabled egress shaping the instance CPU climbed and we saw faster KV cache churn — could be the shaping is causing more prefetch misses?
04:29 Priya Nair: yep shaping reduces tail bandwidth which can increase inter-token latency and cause cache eviction earlier; we can tweak the shaping bucket sizes and increase prefetch window to compensate. We'll suggest two knob changes in the runbook.
04:48 Liam O'Connor: ok last thing — can we get an explicit rollback playbook for kernel upgrades with a low-risk path?
04:55 Alex Ramos: yes, we'll add a rollback playbook with automated canary cutover and a manual toggle, include metric thresholds (p95>120ms or error rate >0.5%) as triggers.
05:10 Jordan Li: I'll own scheduling the canary and coordinate the traffic mirroring, target window Tuesday morning.
05:17 Alex Ramos: awesome. to recap: AB runs across kernel/quantization combos, packet-capture from Crestline, updated telemetry runs, security checklist and runbook changes, and schedule canary next week.
05:30 Jared Vega: thanks all, that's good.
05:35 Alex Ramos: ok we'll follow up in email and drop links to the artifacts — thanks everyone.
